depth_m.note: Applies to the two primary shafts; the OSM names Man Shaft (Downcast) and Rock Shaft (Upcast) match their stated roles (people access, rock/product removal), which is how they are identified here.
depth_m.quote: two 1.1 km primary shafts for people access and rock/product removal, and one 180 m shaft, which is a tailings shaft

geometry.note: OpenStreetMap alone yields at most 'approximate'. Mapped from Bing imagery (source:geometry=Bing); no official shaft diameter was found, so there is no checks[] row.

method: OpenStreetMap way 104138958 (man_made=mineshaft, name 'Man Shaft (Downcast)', 11 vertices, 104 m2) kept verbatim: the shaft collar at the surface. The shaft runs vertically to about 1.1 km; the OSM name matches one of the two primary shafts that the Boulby workshop summary describes as 'two 1.1 km primary shafts for people access and rock/product removal'.
name: Boulby mine Man Shaft (Downcast) (shaft collar, OpenStreetMap)
notes: The third (tailings) shaft, 180 m deep, is not mapped in OSM and is not drawn.

summary.plain: The collar of the mine's people shaft at the surface; the shaft descends about 1.1 km to the level of the underground laboratory.
